newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds slip but spread to Germany narrows.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds slip but spread to Germany narrows.

text.p: Danish state bond prices edged down in thin trade on Tuesday but the 10-year spread to the German bund narrowed nonetheless.
At 1155 GMT the tone-setting seven percent government bond due 2007 was down 0.03 point from Monday's close, to 106.40, yielding 6.14 percent, in turnover of around one billion crowns.
But its spread to the 10-year German bund closed to 57 basis points from Monday's 59 bp.
The outgoing benchmark eight percent bond due in 2006 was down 0.02 point, to 113.60, yielding 5.94 percent, in turnover also of around on billion crowns.
The crown weakened slightly, to 3.8081 to the mark from 3.8075.
The 2006 bond's September future rose 0.02 point to 112.98 while the six percent mortgage-backed bond maturing in 2026 fell 0.32 to 91.83.
The central bank sold 100 million crowns worth of its seven percent 2007, after selling 300 million in the paper on Monday. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
